audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-3 disagreed across layers: content win[0..3] read 'Xerath' (matching packet.levelChart) while full-layer phases[0..3].side all read 'Skill', and the whys under them described Lux chipping him freely.
audit.why: Arcanopulse charges out past Lux's 1100 E, Eye of Destruction lands at 1000 with a slow, and Shocking Orb reaches 1050. Before level 6 Lux has no answer that outranges him, which is what the 48.85% win rate reflects. From 6 the lane evens because Final Spark reaches 3340 and Light Binding cancels his channelled ult.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side moved to 'Xerath' with ratings dropped to 4/10 and all four whys rewritten to describe HIM winning; phases[4..6].why rewritten to explain the even stages. No content win[N] edit is proposed because win[0..3] already read 'Xerath' — a before==after edit would be refused.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named only Lux's item timings and missed the single spike that changes this lane — level 6.
audit.why: Level 6 is the swing because Rite of the Arcane is a 130/115/100s channel that immobilizes Xerath, and Light Binding cancels it outright. Before 6 Lux has no way to touch him; after 6 she holds the answer to his biggest cooldown.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes, phases[4].why, whys[4] and dosFull[2].d now state the level 6 cancel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was nowhere on the page: Xerath's Rite of the Arcane is a channel and Lux's Light Binding cancels it. spikes[1].text says only 'snipe him mid-Rite of the Arcane', which is about damage, not the interrupt.
audit.why: Riot's kit flags R as a channel and the brief's missing-interaction rule states Q cancels it. It is a 130-second cooldown at rank 1 — the single most punishable resource either champion has. Xerath also has no dash of any kind, so a 1175 root on him is unavoidable once he is committed.
audit.corrected: Added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why, whys[4], dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.mid.

audit.why: Shocking Orb at 13s rank 1 / 11s maxed is the window that decides every walk-up, and Rite of the Arcane at 130s is the cooldown worth cancelling.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Shocking Orb, Arcanopulse and both Lux cooldowns as real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d did not answer their own titles, and dontsFull[0].d used 'they' for a single male enemy. report[10].t contained 'ping your jungler every Mantra' — Karma's mechanic leaked onto Lux's page.
audit.why: Templates and bleed, not matchup facts.
audit.corrected: All six bodies rewritten against their titles using Xerath's real ranges and cooldowns; Mantra replaced with the 60-second Final Spark cycle.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jungle influence was only implied by wants.you[1]; breakdown.mid gave the generic 'hover the river' line.
audit.why: Xerath has no dash and no mobility spell in his kit at all, and his ult roots him in place. He is the single easiest gank target in the lane, and Lux's 1175 root converts any jungler's arrival.
audit.corrected: breakdown.mid rewritten around setting up ganks and holding Q for his channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED: the body was the tradeBad string verbatim under an unrelated title.
audit.why: An earlier proposal targeted these same fields but its replacement text overshot the +/-10% length rule, so apply-proposals dropped the edit and the defect survived on disk.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to the same meaning inside the length budget, grounded in real ability names and cooldowns from champ-data/_kits: dontsFull[2].d.

edits.after: Level 1 is his: Arcanopulse charges out past your 1100 E, so he chips your last-hits and you cannot answer.

edits.before: Q joins: the root threat re-prices every step he takes past the wave's midline.

edits.after: Xerath

edits.before: Full kit: Q-E-auto with the passive detonations is a real chunk. Shield his answer and walk.
edits.after: His range keeps denying farm; Shocking Orb is 13 seconds, and only its downtime lets you walk up.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Xerath

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for his aggression, not yours.
edits.after: Poke-dominant levels for him — hold the wave near tower, bank Manaflow, and wait for your R at 6.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Final Spark online at 3340, and Light Binding cancels Rite of the Arcane outright — a 130-second ult.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes squishies from root range. Force him to dodge or die on every contact.
edits.after: Luden's spike: he is immobile and squishy, so one landed Q into full combo is lethal — as is his stun.

edits.before: Late Lux decides fights from a screen away: root the entry, slow the pit, and laser the clump your team froze.
edits.after: An artillery mirror: whoever lands first wins, and his only lockdown is an 11-second Shocking Orb.

edits.before: Level 6 evens: your R matches his range and threatens his immobile frame.
edits.after: Level 6 evens: your Q cancels Rite of the Arcane and your R reaches his frame.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Prismatic Barrier for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb: 13s at rank 1, 11s maxed — his only CC, so dodge it and the artillery never converts; the 11 seconds after are your walk-up window. - Arcanopulse is 9s early, 5s maxed. - Your Q is 10s and cancels his 130-second R mid-channel.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: E reaches 1100 and lingers as a slow zone — drop it on his farm spot so he either gives up CS or eats the detonation.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Every spell charges Illumination; the follow-up auto ignites it for bonus magic damage, so take one auto after each E detonation.

edits.before: Xerath spends Shocking Orb (Stun) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Bank Q for his Rite of the Arcane — the binding cancels the channel and wastes a 130-second ult.

edits.before: That’s Xerath’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Q is 10 seconds; miss it and he stuns you with an orb you no longer threaten.

edits.before: Your W answers exactly one combo per fight — shield the spell that kills, not the one that stings.
edits.after: Your E is 10 seconds and your only safe farm tool — with it down, hold the tower line, don't contest.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 — spend it on a wave and it is missing when Rite of the Arcane opens from 5000 units out.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by chipping you off the wave from outside 1100, then converting one Shocking Orb into his full artillery combo.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Xerath off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt the immobile frame: he has no dash at all, so flank through fog, root him at 1175, and take every fight in the 130 seconds after his ult.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by punishing an immobile artillery mage: one 1175 root on a champion with no dash is the whole combo, and that same Q deletes his ult.

edits.before: Chip with E and the passive weave — your poke is honest and your root threat is the law. Bank Manaflow; the laser runs on it.
edits.after: Farm from range and respect his: Arcanopulse charges out past your E, so take the safe CS, bank Manaflow, and wait for 6.

edits.before: Luden's onward, every root is a kill: shove, hover the river, and Q-R the first contest. Your range decides objective setups alone.
edits.after: From 6 you hold an answer: bank Q for his Rite of the Arcane channel, shove, and set up ganks — no dash makes him the easiest target on the map.

edits.before: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push that crashes on your roam-or-recall timer — the slow zone makes the crash safe to set up. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Q down — the immobile root-bot walking up to farm is mid's most quoted death. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: an E-cleared slow push crashed on your recall timer — his W clears at 1000, so contest the crash with E, not with autos. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with Q down, where Arcanopulse hits you and the minions in one line. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam.

edits.before: If Xerath takes first blood, tighten up: Shocking Orb (Stun) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: If Xerath takes first blood, tighten up: his poke range means you farm from tower and give up the crash. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn't — E-farm and play for his ult channel.

edits.before: Lost Chapter steadies the chip; level 6 turns roots into kills; Luden's makes Q-E-R a deletion.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies mana; 6 gives you a cancel for his ult; Luden's makes one root lethal.

edits.before: You are the longest 'no' in the game: root the engage, slow the pit, and laser whatever your team's front line holds still.
edits.after: Late this is an artillery mirror won by angles: hold Q for whoever steps first and for his channel, and never stand in a straight line.

edits.before: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler every Mantra... every laser cycle.
edits.after: Q-E on arrival is a guaranteed gank: root, slow, detonate. Post-6 your R cleans the Flash they burn — ping your jungler on every 60-second laser cycle.

notes: Chart: content win[] already matched packet.levelChart; only the full layer was stuck on 'Skill' for rows 0-3. Moved the full layer to match, so no paired win[N] edits exist. I deliberately did NOT quote a number for Arcanopulse's maximum range: Riot's kit file lists 750, which is its base cast range, and the beam extends while charging — the file does not give the charged figure, so the page says 'charges out past your 1100 E' rather than inventing a value. Same reasoning for Rite of the Arcane: I used the 5000 range and 130s cooldown from the kit but made no claim about how many barrages or their individual damage. | COHERENCE: 1 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair. QA re-scope: previous edits to dontsFull[2].d were rejected for length drift; re-proposed within budget. Cooldowns quoted are Riot per-rank values from the kit files; no spell-shield, cleanse or minion-block behaviour is asserted anywhere, since the kits do not state it.
